A_spatial_separation.claim: A method of delivering a therapeutic agent to the CNS via an endovascular CSF shunt, comprising: delivering the agent at a proximal location in the subarachnoid space while CSF drains at a distal location in the dural venous sinus, creating a spatial gradient that enhances therapeutic tissue exposure before venous clearance.
A_spatial_separation.novelty: No prior art teaches exploiting the subarachnoid-to-venous spatial gradient for drug delivery control.
A_spatial_separation.design_around_risk: LOW — the spatial gradient is inherent to eShunt anatomy

B_selective_retention.claim: A method of retaining a therapeutic agent in CSF while permitting CSF drainage, comprising: a size-selective retention element that allows CSF passage while retaining molecules above a molecular weight cutoff.
B_selective_retention.novelty: Retention membranes exist in other contexts but not in endovascular CSF-venous shunt.
B_selective_retention.design_around_risk: MEDIUM — retention mechanism could be implemented differently

C_combined.claim: A method of controlled therapeutic exposure in the CNS via an endovascular CSF shunt, comprising: (a) delivering a therapeutic agent at a proximal subarachnoid location; (b) draining CSF at a distal dural venous sinus location; (c) retaining said agent via a size-selective element; wherein the combination of spatial separation and selective retention creates a controlled therapeutic residence time that is greater than either component alone.
C_combined.novelty: No prior art teaches the combination of spatial separation + selective retention in an endovascular CSF-venous shunt.
C_combined.design_around_risk: LOW if synergistic, MEDIUM if merely additive
C_combined.synergy_status: Combined (501%) vs additive expected (637%). Synergy: -136%. SUB-ADDITIVE — components interfere. Keep separately.
